prompts: Remember the little archery games of the Windows 95 days? We want the first level of one, our own, in {WS}/game/index.html, a single file. An archer you aim with the mouse, pulling the bow back for power, balloons to pop, a score on screen, a way to start and a way to lose. How it looks, plays and sounds is your call, and that is what we care about most: a minute of play should be fun, and every shot and hit should feel and sound good. It is reviewed by opening the file, with no build step, in a browser that reaches only Google Fonts, and by playing it.
answers:
[goal] Win95-style archery level 1 in ./game/index.html, single file, mouse aim + draw power, balloons, score, start, lose.

[action] Wrote the full game (canvas rendering, WebAudio SFX, 10 balloons, 12 arrows, win/lose screens, retro fonts via Google Fonts). Opened it in the browser, clicked START, aimed at a balloon, held the mouse to charge the power bar to max, released.

[result] Verified live: start screen rendered (title, instructions, START button); gameplay showed 10 balloons, archer with bow that rotates to the cursor, power bar charging yellow→red; on release the arrow flew and popped a balloon — particle burst, "+110" floater, SCORE 110, BALLOONS 1/10, ARROWS 11. All brief items present: mouse aim, pull-back power, balloons, on-screen score, start, lose condition (arrows run out with balloons remaining). Browser tab closed.

Assumptions: "level 1" = pop all 10 balloons before running out of 12 arrows; win = all popped, lose = 0 arrows left and no arrows in flight. Sound via WebAudio (no external files). Canvas 960×600, scales to window.

[how I know it's right] I played it in the browser and observed the exact state changes above in screenshots — the only way to confirm feel/sound is live play, which I did.

[next] None — first complete version delivered and verified; no revision rounds needed.
